subject: POC evaluation plan and adjusted scope — BrightRetail
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: POC evaluation plan and adjusted scope — BrightRetail

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our discovery, I wanted to put the proposed POC plan in writing so the team can align on timelines, owners, and success criteria. Below is our suggested baseline and a couple of open questions where we need your confirmation.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: reduce production inference latency for personalized checkout prompts and improve recommendation relevance in the mobile checkout path.
- Secondary goal: lower per-request inference cost without regression in top-line conversion metrics.
- Key stakeholders: Product (Alyssa), Engineering (procurement CC’d), and Ops.

Proposed POC (baseline)
- Duration: 4 weeks of testing after data ingestion and baseline validation (target start: 2026-05-18).
- Success criteria (initial):
  * Latency: 95th percentile inference latency improvement >= 25% on checkout flow under our staging load profile.
  * Quality: Relevance uplift as measured by session-level CTR or NRR (we’ll define exact metric with you) — target: no more than 3% drop, ideally 5%+ uplift.
  * Cost: token/unit inference cost <= $0.06 per request at production-like throughput.
- Evaluation plan: shadow and A/B tests (10% traffic) with logging to shared S3 bucket; weekly syncs to review telemetry and early cutover criteria.
- Owners:
  * Redwood: Camila (solutions) — infra & model tuning; Rishi — perf/eval and cost analysis.
  * BrightRetail: Alyssa — product owner; procurement contact for contract prerequisites (cc’d).

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft POC map to this thread (BrightRetail-POC-MAP.xlsx) with task-level owners and data requirements.

Open questions / asks
1) Can you confirm the expected start date and the BrightRetail engineer who will provide dataset access?
2) Is the checkout flow sample size of ~50k impressions per day (staging) representative for the test?
3) Any must-have security/compliance docs we should surface ahead of the Private deployment discussion?

If that looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff (30–45 min) and get Camila to scope infra needs. Thanks — happy to adjust.

Best,

Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
From: Alyssa Moore <alyssa@brightretail.com>

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC evaluation plan and adjusted scope — BrightRetail

Thanks Jonas — really helpful write-up. Quick clarifications and a slight scope change from Product: we want to include a second use case in the POC focused specifically on checkout latency reduction for the mobile web checkout microflow (this is distinct from recommendation relevance).

A couple specifics:
- For the new use case we need the metric to be 95th percentile end-to-end latency (including our client-side time to render) — target: 30% improvement.
- We can provide a sample dataset and a staging token service, but I need Rishi/Camila to confirm what format you need and any schema constraints.
- Procurement asked to see our SOC2 checklist and a short statement on data handling — I’ve looped contracts for timing; they may come back with a standard questionnaire.

We’re still ok with a mid-May start but adding the extra use case likely pushes validation out by ~1–2 weeks depending on data handoff. Please include that estimate in the updated plan.

On the positive side, if we hit the latency target for mobile checkout, Product will prioritize the customer-facing rollout.

Onboarding next steps: once you confirm acceptance of the additional use case, procurement will prepare an SOW addendum and our engineering lead will share access.

Appreciate it — Alyssa Moore
Product Lead, BrightRetail
alyssa@brightretail.com

Subject: Re: POC evaluation plan and adjusted scope — BrightRetail

Thanks Alyssa — scope change understood and reasonable. I’ve sketched an adjusted POC plan below that re-baselines success criteria, timeline, and ownership to account for the additional mobile checkout latency use case. Please review and confirm so we can lock dates and have procurement begin the SOW addendum.

Re-baselined POC plan (updated)
- New duration: 6 weeks total (2 weeks onboarding/data ingest + 4 weeks of evaluation). Proposed window: 2026-05-18 through 2026-06-28.
- Success criteria (updated):
  1) Mobile checkout latency: 95th percentile absolute end-to-end improvement >= 30% over baseline (measured with our synthetic client-side tracer + BrightRetail staging logs).
  2) Recommendation relevance (checkout recommendations): maintain or improve session CTR (max permitted drop: 2%). If recommendation quality drops, we will freeze recommendation model changes and focus on latency path.
  3) Cost: per-request inference unit cost not to exceed $0.05 at the tested throughput; if cost higher, we’ll provide quantization/architecture recommendations and a follow-up test.
- Evaluation methodology:
  * Week 0–2: data ingest, KV cache warmup, baseline collection (we’ll run a set of short synthetic traces to validate measurement instrumentation).
  * Week 3–6: split-run A/B (10–15% traffic) and concentrated stress window (to validate tail latency). Weekly telemetry dumps to shared S3 + Grafana dashboard link (we’ll provide read-only access).
  * Acceptance: pass on mobile latency AND either meet cost target OR demonstrate a clear, actionable plan to reach it within 2 additional weeks.
- Owners and responsibilities:
  * BrightRetail: Alyssa (product owner), BrightRetail Eng (data access + client-side tracer integration), contracts@brightretail.com (SOW).
  * Redwood: Camila (technical lead for setup/tuning), Rishi (perf telemetry and cost acceptance), Jonas (commercial/exec sponsor).

Security/compliance docs
- I attached a SOC2 checklist we typically provide during POC intake (SOC2-Checklist.pdf) and a short data handling blurb. If procurement needs additional items, please send the questionnaire and we’ll prioritize.

Attachments & links
- Attached: SOC2-Checklist.pdf
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3BrightRetailPOC (proposed dashboards and shared S3 path)

Open items
1) Alyssa: confirm the staging dataset format (CSV vs Parquet) and expected handoff date.
2) Procurement: expected contract turnaround for a small SOW addendum (estimate in days).
3) Engineering: we’ll need a contact for client-side tracer integration (name + Slack handle).

If that aligns I’ll update the POC worksheet and we can schedule a kickoff for next Tuesday (2026-05-18) AM slot.

Thanks — Camila
